title: Quasi-finite at a point implies isolated in the fibre
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $x\in X$, put $s=f(x)$, and let $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ be the fibre of $f$ at $s$ with first projection $p:X_s\to X$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. If $f$ is quasi-finite at $x$ [pqf-def-quasifinite], then the unique point $\xi\in X_s$ with $p(\xi)=x$ is isolated in $X_s$: $\{\xi\}$ is open in $X_s$. Equivalently, $\{x\}$ is open in the subspace $f^{-1}(s)$ of $X$. (Stacks Project, Morphisms, Lemma 01TH (lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize), (1) implies (2).)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01TH (lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize), line 3664, first paragraph of the proof ((1) implies (2)); Definition 01TD (definition-quasi-finite), line 3538

proof.text: *Affine charts.* Since $f$ is quasi-finite at $x$ [pqf-def-quasifinite] (Stacks 01TD (1)), there are an affine open $U\subseteq X$ with $x\in U$, an affine open $V\subseteq S$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$, and isomorphisms $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$, $V\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] such that the restriction $f_U:U\to V$ of $f$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ for a ring map $\varphi:R\to A$ (every morphism of affine schemes is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of a unique ring map) which is of finite type and quasi-finite at the prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$ corresponding to $x$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. Since $f(x)=s\in V$, the point $s$ corresponds to the prime $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ of $R$ (the map $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ sends $\mathfrak q$ to $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$). Let $F=A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $j:A\to F$, $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, and $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ the prime of $F$ with $j^{-1}(\overline{\mathfrak q})=\mathfrak q$; by definition of quasi-finiteness at $\mathfrak q$, $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}F$.

source.place: Morphisms, Definition Tag 01TD (1), line 3538, and the proof of Lemma 01TH, line 3684 ('By assumption there exist opens U, V such that f(U) in V, x in U and x an isolated point of U_s')

proof.text: *The open piece $p^{-1}(U)$ of $X_s$ is the fibre of $f_U$.* Let $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ with projections $p:X_s\to X$, $q:X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], and $c:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ the canonical morphism. The residue field of the open subscheme $V$ at $s$ is $\kappa(s)$ and the canonical morphism $c_V:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to V$ satisfies $\iota_V\circ c_V=c$ for the inclusion $\iota_V:V\hookrightarrow S$ [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] (the residue map of an open immersion is an isomorphism). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] to $f$, $c$ and the opens $U\subseteq X$, $V\subseteq S$, $W=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ (so $f(U)\subseteq V$, $c(W)=\{s\}\subseteq V$): the canonical morphism $U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to X_s$, where the fibre product is taken over $f_U$ and $c_V$, is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] with image $p^{-1}(U)\cap q^{-1}(W)=p^{-1}(U)$, compatibly with the projections: it carries the first projection $U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to U$ to $p$ restricted to $p^{-1}(U)$.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma 01TH, lines 3686-3688 ('Since U_s = U \cap X_s \subset X_s is also open'), written out

proof.text: *The fibre of $f_U$ is $\operatorname{Spec}F$.* Let $\pi:R\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ be the canonical map. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification] there is an isomorphism $e:\kappa(s)=\kappa_{\operatorname{Spec}R}(\mathfrak p)\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ with $c_V=\operatorname{Spec}(e^{-1}\circ\pi)=\operatorname{Spec}(\pi)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(e^{-1})$, $\operatorname{Spec}(e^{-1})$ an isomorphism of schemes. Hence $U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, the fibre product of $f_U$ and $c_V$, is with the same first projection a fibre product of $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\pi$ (compose its second projection with the isomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}(e^{-1})$; the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] is unchanged). By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $\operatorname{Spec}A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))=\operatorname{Spec}F$ with first projection $\operatorname{Spec}(j)$. By uniqueness of fibre products up to unique isomorphism over the factors [def-pc-fibre-product] and step 2, there is a homeomorphism $h:\operatorname{Spec}F\to p^{-1}(U)$ onto the open subset $p^{-1}(U)$ of $X_s$ with $p\circ h=\iota_U\circ\operatorname{Spec}(j)$ (under $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$), where $\iota_U:U\hookrightarrow X$.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma 01TH, lines 3684-3688 (U_s is the fibre of U -> V; cf. the third paragraph, lines 3707-3712, 'Spec(\overline A) is an open subscheme of the fibre X_s'), written out

proof.text: *The point $\xi$ and openness.* Let $\xi\in X_s$ be a point with $p(\xi)=x$ (by [def-pc-scheme-fibre] $p$ is a homeomorphism of $X_s$ onto the subspace $f^{-1}(s)$ of $X$, which contains $x$; so $\xi$ exists and is unique). Since $x\in U$, $\xi\in p^{-1}(U)$, so $\xi=h(\mathfrak Q)$ for a prime $\mathfrak Q$ of $F$ (step 3), and $\operatorname{Spec}(j)(\mathfrak Q)=j^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)$ is the point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ that $p(\xi)=x$ corresponds to, namely $\mathfrak q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] (injectivity of $\mathfrak Q\mapsto j^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)$), $\mathfrak Q=\overline{\mathfrak q}$. By step 1, $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}F$; as $h$ is a homeomorphism onto $p^{-1}(U)$, $\{\xi\}=h(\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\})$ is open in $p^{-1}(U)$, and since $p^{-1}(U)$ is open in $X_s$ ($p$ is continuous), $\{\xi\}$ is open in $X_s$.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma 01TH, lines 3685-3690 ('Hence {x} \subset U_s is an open subset ... {x} \subset X_s is an open subset also')

proof.text: *The equivalent form.* By [def-pc-scheme-fibre] the first projection $p$ is a homeomorphism of $X_s$ onto the subspace $f^{-1}(s)$ of $X$; it carries $\xi$ to $x$, hence the open set $\{\xi\}$ of $X_s$ to the open set $\{x\}$ of $f^{-1}(s)$, and conversely $p^{-1}(\{x\})=\{\xi\}$. So $\{\xi\}$ open in $X_s$ is equivalent to $\{x\}$ open in $f^{-1}(s)$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01TH (2), line 3672 ('The point x is isolated in X_s', the point of X_s over x identified with x)
